$description: Struct-level golden vectors for the probe struct (test/golden/probe.ts) — every row of the Primitives table composed into one layout, so the boundary check is exercised where it will actually run. post.json, boxes.json and block.json sit beside this file in the same shape.

vectors.name: probe/minimal
vectors.note: 73 bytes: 1 + 32 + 1 + 32 + 1 + 1 + 1 + 1 + 1 + 1 + 1. Every field at its zero value, so the struct's own shape is what the byte count pins.

vectors.name: probe/full
vectors.note: 88 bytes. `amount` is u64-max — the ten bytes that are the sentinel elsewhere and a legal value here. `offset` is -1, the credit.proofSource transfer sentinel.

vectors.name: probe/populated
vectors.note: 166 bytes. Multi-byte label, a two-element ref array, a present option, `amount` at 2^53 (the first value only the bigint path reaches), and a two-byte version — so a field-order error shifts everything after it.

rejects.name: probe/non-minimal-first-field
rejects.note: probe/minimal with `version` written as the padded `80 00` instead of `00`. Decodes to a byte-identical Probe — steps 1 and 2 both pass — and only the re-encode compare separates it.

rejects.name: probe/non-minimal-eighth-field
rejects.note: The same padding on `offset`, 69 bytes in. Buried mid-struct behind two 32-byte fields, which is where a per-field canonicity check would be easiest to forget.

rejects.name: probe/trailing-byte
rejects.note: probe/minimal with one byte appended. Step 2 — the struct is fully satisfied before the input runs out.
